column1: Why must a game engine's architecture decouple simulation time from wall-clock time?
column2: Because the engine must execute at a consistent cadence regardless of workload variance; using fixed timestep integration prevents variable frame rates from introducing non-determinism into physics and gameplay logic.

column1: What is the central architectural invariant of professional gameplay systems engineering?
column2: The simulation must be decoupled from its presentation—the simulation owns no pointers into the renderer, and the renderer only holds a snapshot or read view of simulation state.

column1: Why is 'update-then-render' considered a correctness invariant rather than a performance optimization?
column2: Without strict temporal ordering of update before render, gameplay systems cannot be unit-tested, replayed, or deterministically simulated—all prerequisites for shipping a production game and avoiding networked desync.

column1: State the rendering equation's core conceptual components (Kajiya, 1986).
column2: Outgoing radiance at a surface point equals emitted radiance plus the hemispherical integral of incoming radiance weighted by the BRDF and the cosine of the angle between incoming light direction and surface normal.

column1: Why can't real-time rendering pipelines solve the rendering equation exactly like offline path tracers?
column2: The rendering equation is a recursive Fredholm integral of the second kind requiring infinite light bounce sampling; real-time budgets (milliseconds per frame) cannot afford the millions of rays per pixel that offline Monte Carlo path tracing uses.

column1: Why do GPUs use forward projection/rasterization instead of backward ray tracing as their primary rendering approach?
column2: GPUs are massively parallel SIMT (Single Instruction, Multiple Thread) machines, and rasterization's structure—projecting geometry via matrix transforms and shading fragments with local illumination approximations—maps efficiently to this parallel hardware architecture.

column1: How do real-time renderers approximate indirect (global) illumination given the rendering equation is intractable in real time?
column2: Through separate passes that precompute or approximate light transport at coarser granularity: baked ambient occlusion, precomputed radiance transfer (spherical harmonics), screen-space ambient occlusion (SSAO), or hardware-accelerated ray tracing.

column1: What does the rigid body abstraction assume, and how many degrees of freedom does it collapse per body in 3D space?
column2: It assumes objects are non-deformable masses with fixed internal geometry, collapsing to six degrees of freedom per body: three translational (center of mass) and three rotational (orientation).

column1: Give the formula for transforming a body's local-space inertia tensor into world space, and explain each term.
column2: I_world = R(q) · I_local · R(q)^T, where R(q) is the rotation matrix derived from orientation quaternion q, and I_local is the symmetric positive-definite local inertia tensor.

column1: State Euler's equations governing rotational dynamics in rigid body physics, and explain the significance of the cross-product term.
column2: τ = Iα + ω × (Iω). The cross-product term ω × (Iω) captures gyroscopic effects arising from angular momentum precession.

column1: What is the purpose of the broad phase in collision detection, and what algorithms implement it?
column2: The broad phase culls the quadratic space of potential body pairs (N²/2) down to a small candidate set likely to intersect, using spatial coherence techniques like bounding volume hierarchies, spatial hashing, or sweep-and-prune algorithms.

column1: In the ECS verification lab, what three domains are used to validate a game engine's performance and correctness?
column2: 1) AST/LLVM IR/assembly analysis to verify compiler optimizations like inlining; 2) hardware performance counter and flamegraph profiling to correlate cache miss rates with data layout; 3) ThreadSanitizer/AddressSanitizer to validate memory safety and happens-before ordering across parallel update systems.
